correctness.rationale: Derivation from Yang et al. Eq. (4) is checked with the mass-conservation boundary flux, and all positive-domain parameters are specified. Hyperexponential sufficiency follows from numerator degree <=2k-2, normalization and 2k-1 roots; necessity follows from a full rank (2k-1)-by-2k confluent-Cauchy Jacobian, the double-zero bound and the implicit function theorem preserving positive distinct parameters. General-law uniqueness follows by complex analyticity, integer Laplace moments and the Hausdorff moment theorem; nonidentifiability uses disjoint smooth positive-hazard bump perturbations preserving mass/mean/all finite exponential observations. Explicit infectiousness profiles verify the profile-level limit. Standard-library check.py provides exact-rational example and algebraic inversion checks, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The question is which aspects of the non-Markovian recovery law an experiment varying endemic vaccination intensity can identify. Exact 2k-1 measurements for at most k exponentials and local nonidentifiability with one fewer provide a sharp natural finite observation cutoff; an unrestricted smooth-hazard impossibility and open-interval uniqueness mark the structural limit. This directly informs whether vaccination panels can identify latent immunity-duration heterogeneity, not an unmotivated parameter sample.
